conventions: all *_mm values are millimetres regardless of the file's units
DXF bounds are of centrelines: polyline constant widths are not included
DXF entity counts are of entities as written, before any union or block resolution
Gerber entries have one layer named after the file; `function` is the X2 TF.FileFunction

fixtures.description: Board outline (ROUTE_TOOL_PATH) and copper artwork (TOP_LAYER) with pads, traces, a slot and an annulus.
fixtures.name: board-islands
notes: copper_bounds_mm includes circle radii but not polyline widths (the widest trace stays inside the pads)
the trace on x = 3 overlaps both pads it joins; a union must count them as one island
the inner circle of the annulus is nested in the outer one and must become a hole, not a second island

fixtures.description: Square with a square hole containing a circular island with its own square hole, plus a disjoint triangle and circle.
fixtures.name: nested-holes
notes: even-odd and nonzero-with-orientation must agree here: every contour is a simple loop
the triangle and the small circle are separate top-level regions

fixtures.description: Lines, an arc, an open polyline and an almost-closed square on MARK; one closed rectangle on FILL.
fixtures.name: open-linework
notes: a region operation on MARK must fail with a diagnostic naming the open geometry, never auto-close
the arc is the lower half of a circle; its bounds reach y = 0

fixtures.description: $INSUNITS = 1 (inches): a 1 x 0.5 in rectangle with a 0.1 in radius circle.
fixtures.name: units-inch
notes: importers must convert on read; the UI must show 25.4 x 12.7 mm, not 1 x 0.5

fixtures.description: One block (circle + square) inserted four times: identity, rotated 45 deg, scaled 2x, scaled 0.5x and rotated 90 deg.
fixtures.name: blocks-insert
notes: block entities sit on layer 0 and must inherit the INSERT's layer (PADS)
order of operations is scale, then rotate, then translate

fixtures.description: Top copper of the board fixture as Gerber X2: flashes (C, R, O, C with hole), traces as draws.
fixtures.name: board-F_Cu
notes: geometry matches dxf/board-islands.dxf TOP_LAYER so both import paths must agree
the annulus is one flash of a C aperture with a hole: one island with one hole

fixtures.description: Board outline (25 x 11.3 mm, 1 mm corner radius) drawn with a 0.05 mm aperture.
fixtures.name: board-Edge_Cuts
notes: a draw chain that returns to its start is one closed path; readers must not leave it open
as a named-boundary domain the contour's interior is the board, not the 0.05 mm ring

fixtures.description: Region with clear/dark compositing, step-and-repeat, thermal and outline macros, obround and polygon apertures, an arc draw, an aperture block with rotation.
fixtures.name: features
notes: all features are disjoint, so the total area is the sum of the analytic areas
the clear circle is composited in source order: the later dark circle inside it survives
the thermal area is the annulus minus two 0.5 mm bars (closed-form circle strips)

fixtures.description: Inkscape-style layers MARK (stroked lines, polyline, quadratic Bézier, rotated group), FILL (Bézier circle, even-odd ring, scaled `use` pads) and CLIPPED (rect cut to its right half by a clipPath), 60 x 20 mm with a 1:1 viewBox.
fixtures.name: marking
notes: y is flipped on import: SVG y grows downwards, the model's y grows upwards
the Bézier circle area is exact to the kappa approximation (about 0.03 %), so the test tolerance is 0.05 mm²
usvg geometry is f32: positions reproduce to about 1e-6 mm, areas to about 1e-4 mm²
stroke widths follow the group scale: the rotated line keeps 0.1 mm, the pads' fill is scaled 1.5x

fixtures.description: One page, 432 x 216 pt: an optional-content layer with a stroked square, a red Bézier circle, a black even-odd ring, two green pads from a scaled form XObject, a grey fill cut by a clipping path, plus text and an image that must be diagnosed.
fixtures.name: features
notes: layers are optional-content group names where present, otherwise the paint colour as #rrggbb
the Bézier circle area is exact to the kappa approximation (about 0.03 %)
0.6 green rounds to 0x99; CMYK and gray paints are converted to RGB names the same way
